investigative-question.def: A question that data can answer: it names the population, the variable, what to estimate (such as a proportion or a typical value) and whether the goal is to describe or to find a cause.

census.def: A study that collects data from every member of the population.

observational-study.def: A study that records variables on individuals without imposing any condition on them. A retrospective study looks back at existing records; a prospective study follows individuals forward in time.

experiment.def: A study in which the researcher deliberately imposes conditions on individuals and measures their responses.

survey.def: A sample survey collects data by asking questions of a sample of individuals. It is an observational study.

explanatory-response.def: The explanatory variable may help explain or predict changes in the response variable, the outcome being measured.

confounding.def: A confounding variable is related to both the explanatory and the response variable, so its effect on the response cannot be separated from the explanatory variable’s effect.

causation.def: A cause-and-effect conclusion says that changing the explanatory variable changes the response. It needs an experiment in which chance decides who gets which condition; observational studies cannot rule out confounding.
